standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked in the counted proof at lines 21359-21361
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the approximating modules of the tensor product system are finitely presented.

core_obligations: Present M and N as directed colimits of finitely presented modules and note that the tensor products of the approximating modules are finitely presented and form a directed system with colimit M tensor N (proof lines 21356-21362).

Use the Mittag-Leffler characterisation for both systems to find indices and maps realising the required compatibility, and observe that the tensor products of those maps serve the same purpose for the tensor product system (proof lines 21363-21373).
Apply the characterisation once more to conclude that the tensor product is Mittag-Leffler (proof lines 21374-21376).
proof_roadmap: Approximate both modules by finitely presented pieces and tensor the systems (proof lines 21355-21362).
Tensor the witnessing maps of the characterisation and conclude (proof lines 21363-21377).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the tensor product of two Mittag-Leffler modules over a ring is again Mittag-Leffler (statement lines 21349-21353). The proof does not compute with the definition directly: it presents both modules as directed colimits of finitely presented modules, uses the characterisation of the Mittag-Leffler property for each system to obtain compatible maps between approximating modules, and then observes that the tensor products of those maps witness the property for the tensor product system (proof lines 21355-21377). Taking the tensor product of the witnessing maps is the step that makes the argument go through, and the author writes out the index bookkeeping. H2.
